title: MLB Live PBP — Scoreboard & Play-by-Play
description: Zero-dependency static web app that pulls live MLB game data straight from the public MLB StatsAPI and renders it in a Gameday-style scoreboard, re-implemented from scratch in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with no build step, no frameworks and no API keys. Two views: a scoreboard showing every game for any date with live scores, inning, count, probable pitchers and W/L/S decisions, and a game view showing who is at bat, who is pitching, the count, outs, runners on base, on-deck and in-the-hole hitters, pitch counts, last play, inning-by-inning linescore, full box score and the complete play-by-play timeline with pitch-by-pitch detail. A third surface is devoted to replay: an all-games Replay Feed page pulls review events from every game on the schedule — manager challenges, crew chief reviews, umpire reviews and ABS pitch challenges — with game link, inning, challenging team, reason, outcome, batter/pitcher context and a three-row review score tracker (Before review, Possible after, Actual after) that explicitly refuses to treat the possible score as a prediction, marks Before/Possible as not observed when the page opens only after resolution, and never assigns a later end-of-plate-appearance score to an earlier pitch review. A Runs at Risk mechanism decides from the data rather than the review type whether the call on the field credited runs to the very event under review — a run counts only when the official payload has a runners[] record with details.isScoringEvent true whose details.playIndex matches the reviewed event — and fires once per review with a chime, an optional desktop notification and a persistent banner, never predicting the ruling. Review detection reads the API's own status registry rather than matching the words challenge/review, because that missed crew-chief reviews whose official detailedState is 'Instant Replay'. The challenge counters are the official StatsAPI counters read as-is (review.away/home.used/remaining and gameData.absChallenges.away/home), never counts derived from feed events, never zero-filled when absent, and a used-counter that moves backwards between polls is flagged on the row as an irregularity instead of being silently corrected. A two-sided hit forecast compounds the batter's and pitcher's season rates by log5 with real platoon splits, recent form, head-to-head history, same-game familiarity and the live count into a single probability with a matchup tier and per-driver point adjustments. Auto-refresh runs at 500ms for the full feed with a 250ms status watcher for the whole slate, and a lean play-by-play probe at 250ms while a review is in flight. LIMITATION: the offline test suites run here — 14 of the 15 tools/*-test.mjs suites pass — but tools/smoke-test.mjs reports 8 checks failed in this sandbox because it fetches the live statsapi.mlb.com teams directory, gameStatus registry and review-status projection and this audit environment has no egress to that host, so that result is an environment limit rather than evidence of a repository defect.
